The article declares a former OAuth setup route redirect.

The documented flow creates an OAuth App or GitHub App.
Users authorize the application before their access tokens are passed to the SDK.
Copilot requests use the authenticated user's Copilot subscription.
Each user authenticates with their own GitHub account.
Usage is described as billed to each user's subscription.
Organization and enterprise accounts are described as supported.
This GitHub OAuth pattern does not require the application to handle model-provider API keys.

The runtime reads GITHUB_COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID.
Integration ID is stamped in the Copilot-Integration-Id header on every agent-session request.
The headless launch example supplies an integration environment variable and example port; no process was launched.
The documented default integration ID is copilot-developer-cli.
A stable product integration ID is suggested for attribution and routing.
Integration ID is configured only through an environment variable, not a first-class SDK option.
For SDK-spawned runtimes the integration variable is passed through client environment options.
For external runtimes the integration variable is set on the runtime process.

The isolation table describes model lookup/cache as per-session.
The isolation table describes state as per session ID under COPILOT_HOME.
GitHub identity is per-session when a token is set on the session; the condition must not be omitted.
Tools are explicit in empty mode and ambient in copilot-cli mode.
Empty mode excludes runtime-bundled built-in skills by default but permits explicitly selected built-ins or custom skills.
Host filesystem access remains shared by the runtime process if host tools are available.
Empty mode exposes no ambient OS tools unless the application registers or allows them.
Shared host-process filesystem access is why copilot-cli mode must not be used for multi-user servers.
Empty mode sends an empty includedBuiltinSkills list in the post-create/post-resume options patch.
That empty-mode options patch also contains an empty installedPlugins list.
Selected built-in skills require explicit inclusion, with language-specific casing.
Applications may opt into their own custom skills with skill enablement and directories; empty mode is not an absolute no-skills guarantee.
sessionFs can replace the default COPILOT_HOME session-state storage route.
Session IDs must be unique and encode an application tenant/user boundary.
Access control must precede session resume or deletion.
Isolated CLI per user is presented as strongest process/credential isolation with higher resource cost.
Shared empty-mode CLI is presented as efficient but requires explicit tools, per-session identity and application access checks.
Hybrid cloud/local sessions require workload routing and policy handling; the linked cloud guide is separately scoped.
In the shared pattern the backend authenticates users, selects session IDs, supplies user tokens and provides explicit tools.
A multi-tenancy diagram asset is referenced; no visual review is inferred from the link.
Always use empty mode for the documented shared-runtime pattern.
Use unique session IDs and store ownership metadata in the application database.
Check ownership before session resume, deletion or any UI action referencing a session ID.
Pass a per-session user token when requests should run as that user.
Register only tools the session needs.
Configure an idle timeout and explicitly delete completed workflow sessions.
Source-qualified custom/MCP allowlists are preferred over unspecified tool patterns.
The default CLI-like mode can expose ambient host files, so omission of empty mode is a stated pitfall.
Omitting idle timeout can accumulate inactive sessions in long-running servers.
Sharing a token across users instead of session-scoped tokens is a stated pitfall.
Client-provided session IDs require backend ownership checks.
Connected-client baseDirectory cannot relocate external runtime storage.
Broad builtin:* patterns require review of each tool's user suitability.
Scaling, backend, BYOK, cloud sessions, persistence and feature links remain references, not automatically completed artifact reviews.

groups.decision: User OAuth delegates individual identity/subscription, not model-provider keys. App/secret setup and exchange snippets are inert. Finer-grained GitHub App permissions are recommended; snippets do not demonstrate state validation or complete secure OAuth. Broad permission handlers and diagram links confer neither authorization nor asset review.

The application owns OAuth storage/refresh/expiry and membership authorization. Membership snippets do not demonstrate pagination/status/permission completeness. Existing cached clients do not demonstrate credential rotation. EMU source enforcement claims are not target verification.

Empty mode is required for shared servers by the source, with explicit tools, scoped identity and application ownership checks. Existing runtime connections ignore client home/timeout settings; language examples, approve_all and absent transport token are not secure-service proof.

State-directory, idle timeout and environment configuration belong to the spawned or external runtime owner as applicable. Timeout values are tunable examples. Custom filesystem providers require tenant-aware paths; upstream verified-surface wording and Java limitations remain source-scoped, not local runtime certification.

Per-session identity differs from process credentials. Intentionally shared service-account semantics must be explicit. Integration IDs are environment-only attribution/routing metadata, not authorization or billing proof.

Session state/model cache isolation is conditional; host files are shared when host tools exist. Empty mode excludes default skills/plugins but selected/custom skills may be available. IDs do not authorize: ownership checks precede resume/delete/UI access. Allowlist, cleanup and timeout source rules require actual approved target verification.

Actions built-in tokens differ from external App installation tokens. All repositories installation access and repository_ids mint requests are separate conditions, not contradictory scopes. Organization policy and Copilot write permission are prerequisites. Installation tokens must use runtime environment rather than SDK user-token options. Checkout version tags remain examples, not immutable-action policy.

Child examples pass credentials through environment and disable stored-user fallback; absence/null/falsy checks differ and do not validate tokens. FFI requires host environment before runtime load; existing URI requires runtime-process environment, not connected-client overrides.

Installation tokens expire after one hour: mint before expiry and restart the appropriate child client or host runtime. This differs from user-session preflight refresh and BYOK provider callbacks. Installation owner determines usage attribution/billing; token route, request scopes, organization policy and runtime/model availability require independent observations.

findings.description: Current caveat already excludes pagination/error/permission completeness; additionally make response-status/type checking absence explicit. A first-page membership match is not exhaustive role/membership authorization.
findings.correction: Clarify example does not inspect HTTP status or validate response array shape; no need to invent a source-required status API.

important_preserved_limits: OAuth application lifecycle versus session token-provider registration is correctly separated; callbacks do not transfer OAuth refresh ownership to SDK.
Client cache creates only absent users; credential rotation for an existing cached client is correctly unproven.
External-runtime client baseDirectory is explicitly ignored; timeout responsibility stays external runtime owner. Example900second values are not required universal thresholds.
Python approve_all and Rust connection_token None are retained as examples, not authorization or secure remote-transport proof.
Organization membership snippet does not demonstrate pagination, role checks, permission completeness or target enforcement; EMU IP/SAML attribution remains source-only.
Integration IDs are routing/attribution metadata, not authority or billing proof.
Filesystem sharing remains conditional on host tools; empty mode does not imply absolute absence of selected/custom skills.
Diagram references do not establish actual image inspection.
